## Space out touching parcels on a running belt before they reach the scanner
이 제출물 참고해서,
우리는 컨베이어 벨트 위에서 박스가 지나가는 과정에서,
박스가 열려 있는 경우는 불량품으로 판단해서 컨베이어 벨트에서 빼고,
그렇지 않은 건 통과하도록 하는 task는 어떨까?
먼저 기존 제출물 한번 참고해볼래?

좋아. 그러면 열린 박스는 플랩을 피해 몸통을 잡고 내용물을 흘리지 않게 빼내고,
닫힌 박스는 그대로 통과시키는 방향으로 구체화해봐. 기존 태스크와 차별점, 채점 기준, 구현 순서까지 정리해줘.

[$robocurve-workflow](/Users/dennis0405/Workspace/SNU-PI/robocurve/automation/skills/robocurve-workflow/SKILL.md) 이거 참고해서 진행하도록 해.
다만 아이디어 자체는 지금 방향으로 확정해서 작업 진행해보자.

실행 범위
- 이 run은 새 과제다. 기존 snack-bag 및 다른 산업 과제의 run/branch/worker를 변경하거나 종료하지 않는다. 다른 run이 등록 GPU를 소유하면 건드리지 말고 실제 자원 충돌을 보고한다.
- 아이디어는 '열린 상자의 플랩을 피해 몸통을 파지하고 자유 내용물을 보존하며 이동 벨트에서 불량품 트레이로 옮김; 닫힌 정상 상자는 벨트에서 그대로 통과'로 고정한다. 다른 산업 작업군으로 바꾸거나 여러 무관한 후보를 탐색하지 않는다. 이 방향 안에서 형상, 배치, 플랩 상태, 속도 등을 물리적으로 실행 가능하게 조정할 수 있다.
- 최종 목적은 분류 설명 자체보다 상태에 맞는 정밀 조작을 평가하는 것이다. 색깔만 바꾼 pick-and-place와 실제 능력이 같은지 엄격히 확인한다. 산업 설정과 신규성은 별개다. 중복 판정을 억지로 통과시키지 않고 구체적 근거와 해결하지 못한 부분을 보고한다.
- 작업 방식은 공용 task.py / YAM / 실제 pinned runtime. 새 연성 솔버 연구는 하지 않는다. 강체 상자 몸통, 유한 두께의 실제 충돌 플랩과 관절, 자유롭게 움직이는 내용물로 시작한다.

2. PR83 Add conveyor block sorting task는 최종 거절 후 closed/unmerged. 색깔 큐브의 벨트 선택/분류는 기존 RoboDojo와 겹친다는 공식 거절 사유가 있다. 캐시 HTML 상태보다 실제 GitHub 상태/공식 댓글을 우선한다.
   https://github.com/robocurve/benchmark-tasks/pull/83

3. 원문 비교 필수:
   https://robodojo-benchmark.com/doc/sim-tasks/match-and-pick-from-conveyor/
   https://robodojo-benchmark.com/doc/sim-tasks/pick-from-conveyor-by-image/
   PR910 conveyor-photo-build 및 다른 moving conveyor selection 과제도 비교한다.
- 원래 작업과의 구분 후보는 '움직이는 개방 플랩의 간섭 회피 + 몸통 파지 + 내부 자유 내용물의 유출 방지 + 정상품에 개입하지 않고 라인 통과'의 물리적 결합이다. 플랩과 내용물이 장식에 그치면 차별점으로 주장하지 않는다. 전수 제출/팀 이력/6개 지정 벤치마크 비교를 유지한다.

명세·채점 설계 지침 (아래 수치 제안은 사용자 확정치가 아닌 검증할 초기안)
- 예시 지시문: Remove the open cartons to the reject tray without spilling their contents. Let the closed cartons continue down the belt.
- YAM 파지 폭을 실제 모델에서 확인. 예를 들어 길이120mm x 폭80mm x 높이70mm의 몸통은 시작점일 뿐이며 플랩 간섭, 벽 두께, 자유 파지면, 그리퍼 여유를 실제 충돌 모델로 검증한다.
- 상자는 바닥과4개 벽의 열린 내부를 가진 compound rigid geometry; 열린 플랩은 회전관절/실제 충돌 형상. 닫힌 상태의 유지 장치는 명시한다. 필수 충돌 제거, 가짜 손-상자 weld, 내용물 고정, pose/velocity 덮어쓰기, 순간이동으로 성공을 만들지 않는다. 정상적인 벨트 표면 속도 구현과 상자 속도 강제주입은 구분한다.
- 내용물은 셀 수 있는 자유 강체 몇 개로 시작한다. 실제 내부 공간/출구와 물체 형상에 기반한 유출 판정. 일단 유출한 뒤 다시 주워 넣어도 유출 이력은 지워지지 않는다.
- 정상/불량 라벨은 시작 시 실제 폐쇄 상태에 고정한다. 로봇이 뚜껑을 닫거나 정상품을 열어서 라벨을 바꿀 수 없다. 불량을 닫아 통과시키기는 이 과제의 제거 성공이 아니다.
- 불량 성공: 제한 시간 내 reject tray에 몸통과 내용물이 함께 안정적으로 놓이고 손을 완전히 뗀 상태로3초 유지. 플랩만 집거나 테이블/바닥으로 밀어 떨어뜨리는 것은 성공이 아니다. 몸통 파지는 실제 양측 접촉/지지 위치와 원시 trace로 검증하며 물리적으로 동등하게 유효한 전략은 설명 없이 배제하지 않는다.
- 정상 성공: 원래 벨트 경로로 downstream 판정선을 통과. 잠깐 벨트 밖으로 꺼냈다 복귀하거나 라인을 장시간 막아도 통과하도록 만들지 않는다. 무접촉 통과 대조군의 실제 마찰/속도 기반으로 충분한 시간 여유를 정한다.
- 판정은 매 제어 주기 이력을 누적해 유출/잘못된 정상품 제거/낙하/라인 정지/누락을 잡는다. 초기점수0, 중간 진행과 최종 성공을 구분. 부분점수와 전역 실패 조건이 모순되지 않도록 계약에서 명확히 정한다. 단일 실패가 모든 부분점수를 무조건 지워 변별력을 없애는지 검토한다.
- 개방 플랩 회피가 실제 필요한지, 내용물을 무시한 거친 이동과 정밀 이동의 결과가 다른지, 전부 제거/전부 방치하는 정책이 만점을 못 받는지 대조군으로 확인한다.

구현 순서와 통과 조건
1. 산업 포장 검사/불량 배출 근거와 원문 비교, 이 아이디어의 명세·채점·라이선스 고정. 새로운 무관한 후보 탐색으로 돌리지 않는다.
2. 정지한 열린 상자1개: 실제 YAM 몸통 파지 -> 들어 올리기 ->3초 유지. 자유 내용물/플랩 실제 충돌 유지. 이 단계가 실패하면 벨트나 여러 상자를 추가하지 않는다.
3. 정지 상자1개를 reject tray로 옮겨 내려놓고 그리퍼 해제 후3초 유지. 무조작/플랩 파지/잘못된 파지/기울여 유출/낙하 대조군과 채점 검증.
4. 마찰 기반 움직이는 벨트에 열린 상자1개. 추종, 파지, 수직 분리, 안전한 수평 이동과 트레이 안착. 속도를 낮춰도 되지만 실제 제한과 이유를 기록.
5. 닫힌 상자의 무개입 통과와 물리/채점 대조군 검증 후 열린·닫힌 혼합 스트림. 확장보다 완결 가능한 작은 장면을 우선하며 배치/순서/플랩 초기조건을 명세한다.
6. 같은 최종 소스의 두 번 독립 fresh-process full-score YAM 데모, 실패/부분점수 대조군, raw action/body/joint/score trace와 독립 재채점, 장면/최종/데모 영상, 깨끗한 환경 이식 확인. 미검증 결과를 만들어 보고하지 않는다.
7. 모든 제작 게이트 후에만 trusted coordinator의 Dream 최종 episode1회와 누적20USD ledger. 실패/결과불명에도 자동 새 episode 금지. 키를 역할 에이전트에 넘기지 않는다.
8. 별도 run origin branch에 코드·에셋·재현 명령·라이선스·최종 영상·주요 측정을 보존하고 실제 compute 상태를 보고. 50MB/file 또는100MB checkpoint 초과는 업로드 전 설명한다.
9. review report.html, release-manifest digest와 실제 영상으로 사용자 검토. 구체적 검토 버전의 별도 승인 전 공식 미디어 업로드/대회 PR/최종 제출은 하지 않는다.

comparisons.objective: Dry all exposed and hidden regions of long articulated hair with a handheld dryer, then switch off, park, and release it while the head remains fixed.
comparisons.physical_skill: Dryer pickup and switch operation, airflow aiming, thermal control, and manipulation of flexible hair bundles to expose occluded layers.
comparisons.success_condition: Every one of 960 patches retains at most 10% water; temperature stays at or below 50°C; hair remains attached, head motion stays within 2 mm/1°, and the powered-off parked dryer and clear hands remain stable for 1 s. A full-task allowance is still unspecified.
comparisons.reason: The candidate tests close-clearance insertion, ball-lock retention, load-bearing lift, three-pad seating, unloading, and pin extraction. Hair exposure and geometry-dependent drying are materially different abilities; generic grasping and parking do not establish overlap.

comparisons.objective: Close the four open flaps of a preloaded carton and seal it using film pulled from an ordinary loose tape roll, then cut and park the tools.
comparisons.physical_skill: Flap folding, thin-film leader manipulation, controlled payout, adhesive application across a seam and end wraps, and guarded cutting.
comparisons.success_condition: Full credit requires contained products, correctly ordered flaps within 5°, one physically connected cut strip bonded across the seam and at least 35 mm down both ends, tools parked, hands clear, carton speed below 10 mm/s, and a 2 s released hold. Tears over 4 mm, drops, over 5% film strain, missing samples, or material-accounting failures invalidate. No task.json or completed native demonstration is present, but scoring thresholds are supplied in source documents.
comparisons.reason: Adhesive-film sourcing, flap closure, bonding, and cutting do not test a mechanical lifting-pin lock or suspended-load transfer. Both involve release-state verification, but that generic primitive is insufficient for overlap.

comparisons.objective: Turn an upright taped carton upside down, cut its bottom tape, open all bottom flaps, collapse the intact carton, and leave it flat.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual turnover of a free carton, guarded blade tracking, articulated flap opening, and controlled wall-tube collapse.
comparisons.success_condition: After a measured 0.5 s inverted hold, all 158 tape cells must be cut; all four bottom flaps must physically reach at least 150°; final full credit requires all eight flaps within 15° of their wall planes, all board vertices in a 24 mm slab with specified heights, speed below 10 mm/s, cutter parked, hands clear, and a 1 s hold. Crease separation, premature forced flap opening, drops, invalid angle history, or cutting before turnover invalidate. No task.json or completed full demonstration is present.
comparisons.reason: Carton turnover, cutting, hinge articulation, and flattening test different force-control and manipulation capabilities from pin insertion, load-bearing ball-lock engagement, suspended-part seating, and unloaded extraction.

comparisons.objective: Safely isolate and depressurize a pneumatic manifold, disconnect its push-to-connect tube, and blank the open port with a retained stem plug.
comparisons.physical_skill: Valve and padlock manipulation, dump-button operation, collet depression with coordinated tube withdrawal, close-tolerance plug insertion, and retention verification.
comparisons.success_condition: Latest full credit requires padlock-before-release and pressure at or below 0.1 bar, tube removal, a released plug seated within 2 mm laterally/3 mm axially and 10° tilt, clearance from arms/tool, a fresh 0.5 s stability window, and survival of a 15 N upward pull for 0.5 s with at most 1 mm displacement; unsafe release is a sticky zero and final success is held 1 s.
comparisons.reason: There is meaningful primitive similarity—actuator depression, axial removal/insertion, and pull-retention testing—but this record tests pneumatic isolation, flexible-tube collet release, and port blanking. The candidate additionally requires a movable shackle to carry a suspended workpiece, align it onto three supports, transfer load, verify support, and only then unlock and recover the lifting pin. That load-transfer ability is not tested here.

comparisons.objective: Depress the latch of a marked Ethernet plug in a crowded panel, withdraw it, relocate it to an empty port, and leave it re-latched without disconnecting six neighboring plugs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Confined latch depression, axial extraction, flexible-cable management, precise plug transfer and reinsertion, and released hook retention.
comparisons.success_condition: The latch must travel at least 1.8 mm before withdrawal; the plug must become disconnected, then seat over 8 mm in the target with under 1 mm lateral error and under 5° angle, latch travel below 0.3 mm, hook retained, neighbors withdrawn no more than 8 mm, hands clear, speed below 10 mm/s, and a 2 s hold. Clip damage, a drop, missing samples, or neighbor disconnection invalidate. No task.json or successful unplug/re-latch demonstration is present.
comparisons.reason: Both tasks include spring-actuated release, axial extraction, reinsertion, and released retention. However, this record tests crowded connector/cable servicing, whereas the candidate's defining ability is certified mechanical load support through a lifting pin, suspended workpiece transport, three-pad seating, load transfer, and support-dependent pin recovery.

comparisons.objective: Lock a used safety needle’s hinged sheath one-handed against a table, then release the syringe inside a sharps tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Safe barrel grasping, surface-reacted hinge rotation, force-controlled snap-latch engagement, needle avoidance, and tray placement.
comparisons.success_condition: The sheath must close around the needle and its sprung catch return within 0.3 mm; the covered syringe must lie fully in the tray, be released and at rest for 1 s. Bare-needle proximity by the wrong gripper, contact with the pad/tray, a drop, or locking without table support is a sticky zero; a 3 N post-run pull must not reopen the sheath.
comparisons.reason: This tests one-handed sharps shielding and hazard avoidance through a hinged snap catch. It does not test close-clearance lifting-pin insertion, axial ball-lock retention under a suspended load, fixture seating, load transfer, or subsequent unlocked pin extraction.

comparisons.objective: Mount the final bicycle-tire bead section without damaging the tube; candidate installs and recovers load-rated lifting hardware while transferring a workpiece.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tire-bead deformation and bimanual pressing versus close-clearance pin insertion, ball locking, shackle lifting, supported seating, and unlocked extraction.
comparisons.success_condition: Bead fully seated, valve aligned, tube undamaged, and hands clear versus verified pin retention, supported lift, three-pad seating, pin removal, clearance, and 3 s dwell.
comparisons.reason: The tasks test deformable tire mounting versus a rigid temporary-lifting-hardware lifecycle; all material rubric details needed for distinction are present.

comparisons.objective: Thread and close a bent-foot U-lock around a bicycle wheel and stand; candidate uses a lifting pin to move and fixture a machined part, then retrieves the pin.
comparisons.physical_skill: Angled two-ended crossbar engagement around obstacles versus axial bore insertion, spring-button actuation, load-bearing ball lock, suspended seating, and extraction.
comparisons.success_condition: U-lock latched around both wheel and stand versus retained-pin pull test, supported lift, three-pad workpiece seating, unloaded pin withdrawal, and stable release.
comparisons.reason: Both manipulate locking mechanisms, but the U-lock tests enclosure and crossbar closure rather than temporary load capture, weight transfer, and hardware recovery; no critical rubric detail is missing.

comparisons.objective: Lower a hoist-suspended motor onto four mounting studs and leave the chain slack; candidate installs a lifting pin, transfers a workpiece onto fixture pads, and removes the pin.
comparisons.physical_skill: Pendant-controlled hoist lowering plus steering a suspended multi-hole load onto studs versus close-clearance pin installation, mechanical retention, shackle lifting, fixture seating, button-held extraction.
comparisons.success_condition: Four motor feet flat over studs with slack chain, released controls, and safety gates versus locked-pin pull resistance, a 30 mm supported lift, three-pad seating, complete pin removal, clearance, and 3 s dwell.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest record because both test suspended-load alignment and support transfer, but the candidate additionally makes installation, load-bearing verification, unlocking, and recovery of temporary lifting hardware the tested mechanism; both rubrics are sufficiently specified.

comparisons.objective: Thread and tighten a spin-on oil filter to a bounded post-contact rotation; candidate locks a lifting pin, transfers a workpiece, and recovers the pin.
comparisons.physical_skill: Controlled threaded rotation and torque/angle stopping versus axial pin alignment, button and ball-lock actuation, suspended-load control, seating, and extraction.
comparisons.success_condition: Filter remains threaded within the allowed tightening-angle band and is released without over-tightening versus staged retention, lift, fixture support, withdrawal, clearance, and dwell checks.
comparisons.reason: Shared guarded force control is generic; threaded tightening and temporary lifting-pin load transfer test different abilities, and no missing numeric detail creates plausible duplication.

comparisons.objective: Take a tympanic temperature with a covered probe and lay the instrument down; candidate transfers a machined part using a self-locking lifting pin.
comparisons.physical_skill: Anatomical probe alignment, button press, and sub-millimetre steady holding versus mechanical pin locking, shackle lifting, fixture seating, and coordinated unlocking and withdrawal.
comparisons.success_condition: Valid reading after a 3 s steady seated hold, safe insertion depth, and released thermometer versus verified lock retention, supported lift, three-pad seating, extracted pin, and 3 s stable clearance.
comparisons.reason: The insertion primitive is shared only generically; medical probing does not test load-bearing retention or support transfer, and both rubrics provide decisive thresholds.

comparisons.objective: Align pipe flanges and insert locating pins; candidate installs a load-bearing lifting pin, moves a workpiece, seats it, and removes the pin.
comparisons.physical_skill: Flange pose alignment and passive locating-pin insertion versus spring-button actuation, radial ball-lock engagement, shackle load control, support verification, and unlocked extraction.
comparisons.success_condition: Aligned flange holes with two or four locating pins in final pose versus pull-tested retention, elevated supported load, three-pad contact, complete pin recovery, clearance, and dwell.
comparisons.reason: This is geometrically similar at insertion, but PR-125 lacks mechanical locking, lifting through the pin, load transfer, and pin recovery; its earlier variants omit release and damage-history criteria, which does not make the objectives duplicative.

comparisons.objective: Align two boards edge-to-edge and clamp them with a trigger bar clamp; candidate fixtures a machined part using temporary lifting hardware.
comparisons.physical_skill: Clamp placement, trigger pumping, board alignment, and force buildup versus pin insertion and locking, shackle lifting, suspended seating, unloading, and extraction.
comparisons.success_condition: Boards closed, aligned, level, and held at at least 20 N after release versus pin retention and lift stages followed by three-pad seating, pin removal, and stable hand clearance.
comparisons.reason: Both involve a spring-operated mechanism and force retention, but clamping a joint does not test temporary lifting, suspended alignment, or hardware recovery; numeric rubrics are available.

comparisons.objective: Release a camera plate from a cam-and-lip mount and place it on a pad; candidate installs and later removes a lifting pin around a load-transfer operation.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rotate a passive cam, clear a rear retaining lip, and support a small payload versus insert and verify a ball lock, lift through a movable shackle, seat a suspended workpiece, and extract the unloaded pin.
comparisons.success_condition: Cam released, payload clear and upright on its pad, no drop, hands clear, and 1 s stable versus retained pin, supported lift, three fixture contacts, complete pin removal, clearance, and 3 s dwell.

last_candidate.title: Screen ceramic finishing media from finished metal washers
last_candidate.objective: Pour a dry mixture of full-scale metal washers and ceramic angle-cut cylinders into a supported manual separating screen, manipulate the screen so the media passes into the collection tray, retain every washer, then release the screen onto its supports.
skills: Bimanual rim grasping and load sharing
Controlled pouring into a supported tool
Tool orientation and oscillation driven by granular flow
Stable placement and release without spilling
last_candidate.success_conditions: Primary score: percentage of starting media mass physically recovered beneath the screen (0–70 points), plus 20 points if every washer remains in the screen and 10 points if the released screen rests on all supports for 3 seconds. Any washer leaving the screen permanently loses the 20 retention points; media crossing the rim, floor contact, or tray escape is immutable loss and cannot earn recovery credit. Washer fracture or permanent deformation is damage and caps the total at 40. Full score requires at least 98% media recovery, 100% washer retention, no recorded rim spill or floor contact, and the released 3-second supported dwell. These outcomes are reproducible with a scale and continuous video; shake count, hand identity, action order, and motion style are not graded.
last_candidate.industrial_value: Raytech identifies screens as equipment for manually separating parts from finishing media and describes hand separation as tedious and labor intensive. The task therefore represents post-finishing material recovery performed by inspectors, testers and sorters, hand laborers/material movers, and production workers rather than color-based conveyor sorting.
last_candidate.dexterity: The 9.525 mm diameter media can enter a 12.7 mm opening end-first, but its 22.225 mm length exceeds the approximately 17.96 mm diagonal of a square opening, creating real orientation-dependent bridging. The robot must coordinate a two-arm grasp, tilt, and bounded agitation while keeping larger annular workpieces inside. A no-motion or simple dump policy should leave bridged media, while excessive motion can cause rim loss or part damage.

evidence.locator: PDF p.21, ceramic media product list
FAQ section, “What is the best way to separate the parts from the media?”

last_candidate.asset_plan: Author a representative full-scale 368.3 mm diameter by 63.5 mm deep polymer screen with finite-thickness walls, a graspable rounded rim, and actual 12.7 mm square apertures; use compound bars or supported triangle-mesh collision so holes remain physically open. Model free rigid 9.525 by 22.225 mm angle-cut ceramic cylinders at the manufacturer’s nominal envelope. Use recognizable annular metal workpieces with a disclosed representative geometry—30 mm outside diameter, 8 mm bore, 4 mm thickness—and measured simulation mass; this is a testable modeling assumption, not an exact product replica. Provide a rigid receiver, two stable screen supports, and a gripper-accessible feed cup. Validate one-media end-first passage, transverse bridging, washer retention in every orientation, multi-body no-op and spill controls, then YAM grasp/lift, pour, sift, support placement, release, and fresh-observation dwell at the pinned 240 Hz physics/10 Hz control runtime. Preserve per-body trajectories, contacts, mass accounting, and 240 Hz collision-check labels separately from grading.
last_candidate.risk: The full-size screen is large relative to the YAM tabletop and requires a verified two-arm reachable rim layout. Dense collections of slender rigid media may exhibit tunneling, unstable contacts, or unrealistic self-locking; aperture passage, bridge release, spill behavior, and screen/support grasp clearance must pass component tests before a full demo. The representative washer geometry must be disclosed clearly so it is not presented as a verified commercial SKU.
